root_cause_label: Repeated sed editing failures corrupting source file due to sed not expanding \n in replacement strings
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent repeatedly used sed with \n in replacement strings to insert multi-line Java code, which sed does not expand as newlines, producing source files with literal 'n' characters and malformed method declarations that would never compile, and despite rollback to a clean state the agent immediately repeated the same broken approach without switching to a reliable editing tool.
t_err_evidence: sed -i '141s/.*/sanitizedFilename.../' FileUploadHandler.java replaces dest Path with String, breaking the resolve call
t_commit_evidence: Step 11 commits the agent to the sed-based multi-line editing approach. After rollback at step 32, the agent immediately retries the same broken strategy at steps 34-35 (sed with \n sequences), demonstrating that the failure mode is locked in from step 11 and that no strategy switch ever occurs throughout the trajectory.
t_surface_evidence: output shows 'n\tprivate String getSanitizedFilename' — stray 'n' persists, confirming malformed insertion
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge that sed does not interpret \n as a newline in replacement strings (using -i and single-quoted patterns on standard shells). Every multi-line insertion via sed produced literal 'n' characters or single malformed lines rather than properly separated Java statements, and the agent never recognized the root cause of this repeated failure.
